about: Research sheet for the Nevada county edition. Every contact below was read on the date in reviewed_on from the page named beside it; scripts/make_county_state.py turns it into the edition files.
name: Nevada
phones_sentence: Veterans office phones and addresses come from the Nevada Department of Veterans Services’ veterans service officer page. Most rural counties have no office; call or use Ask a VSO.

offices.source_title: Nevada Department of Veterans Services: Veterans Service Officers
offices.note: Nevada Department of Veterans Services veterans service officers are accredited by VA and help with claims, pension, survivor benefits and appeals at no charge. The department says intake appointments are taking about 30 to 90 days to schedule.
offices.selection: Office address and phones as printed on the department’s veterans service officer page; fax numbers omitted. A county without an office shows the department’s statewide card.

aging.source_title: Washoe County Senior Services Advisory Board: Nevada Care Connection overview (October 2, 2024)
aging.source_scope: The Nevada Care Connection Resource Center partners, their phones and the counties each serves, and the Medicare Assistance Program line; read in full.
aging.description: The Nevada Care Connection Resource Center for this county: one-on-one help for older adults, people with disabilities and caregivers to explore options, plan for care and connect with services such as meals, help at home and caregiver support. Nevada has no Area Agencies on Aging; these centers are the local starting point.
aging.next_step_extra: You can also dial 2-1-1 and ask for your local Nevada Care Connection Resource Center.

programs.name: Nevada veterans: state veterans service officers for claims help
programs.description: Free help with VA claims, appeals, pension and survivor benefits from the Nevada Department of Veterans Services’ accredited veterans service officers, in offices in Reno, Fallon, Elko, Winnemucca, Pahrump, North Las Vegas and Mesquite.
programs.next_step: Call 775-321-4880 (northern Nevada offices) or 702-224-6025 (Las Vegas), or use Ask a VSO on the department’s website.
constraints: The department says intake appointments are taking about 30 to 90 days to schedule, depending on location.
Most rural counties have no office; call or use Ask a VSO.

sources.title: Nevada Department of Veterans Services: Veterans Service Officers
sources.scope: Office addresses and phones, and the 30-to-90-day intake wait; read in full. The page was last modified July 7, 2026.

programs.name: Nevada Care Connection: aging and disability resource centers
programs.organization: Nevada Aging and Disability Services Division, Nevada Care Connection
programs.description: Nevada Care Connection Resource Centers give one-on-one help to older adults, people with disabilities, caregivers and families: exploring options, planning for care and connecting with services. Military service is not required.
programs.next_step: Dial 2-1-1 and ask for your local Nevada Care Connection Resource Center, or choose a county above for its center.
constraints: Each program has its own eligibility and waitlist.

programs.name: Nevada Long-Term Care Ombudsman and adult abuse reporting
programs.organization: Nevada Aging and Disability Services Division, Long Term Care Ombudsman Program
programs.description: Advocacy for residents of nursing homes and residential facilities for groups and individuals.
programs.next_step: Call the ombudsman helpline at 888-282-1155. To report abuse, neglect or exploitation of a vulnerable adult, call Adult Protective Services at 702-486-6930 in Las Vegas and Clark County or 888-729-0571 elsewhere in Nevada. In an emergency, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing agency.

programs.name: Free legal help for Nevada veterans and older adults
programs.organization: Nevada Legal Services; Legal Aid Center of Southern Nevada; Volunteer Attorneys for Rural Nevadans
programs.description: Nevada Legal Services serves every county and runs a Senior Legal Helpline. The Legal Aid Center of Southern Nevada (Clark County) offers all its services to veterans and works with the Attorney General’s Office of Military Legal Assistance. Volunteer Attorneys for Rural Nevadans covers the rural counties, and the Southern Nevada Senior Law Program serves Clark County residents 60 and older.
programs.next_step: Call the Senior Legal Helpline at 877-693-2163. In Clark County, call the Legal Aid Center of Southern Nevada at 702-386-1070. In rural counties, call Volunteer Attorneys for Rural Nevadans at 866-448-8276. For a lawyer referral, call the State Bar of Nevada at 800-789-5747.
constraints: Legal aid screens by income, case type and county.

programs.name: VA health care systems serving Nevada
programs.description: Nevada veterans are served mainly by the VA Southern Nevada Healthcare System (North Las Vegas VA Medical Center, 6900 North Pecos Road; 702-791-9000) and the VA Sierra Nevada Health Care System (975 Kirman Avenue, Reno; 775-786-7200). Northeastern Nevada, including Elko and Ely, is served by the VA Salt Lake City Health Care System’s clinics.
programs.next_step: Use VA’s facility locator with your ZIP code to find the closest clinic. Not enrolled yet? Ask an NDVS veterans service officer for help applying.
constraints: Which system serves you depends on where you live; VA’s locator shows the right clinic.

coverage_scope: Referral edition. All 17 counties have a Nevada Department of Veterans Services route (seven counties have an office; the other ten use the department’s statewide lines), a Nevada Care Connection Resource Center, the statewide long-term care ombudsman and a Center for Independent Living.
coverage_note: Veterans offices come from the Nevada Department of Veterans Services’ veterans service officer page; ten counties have no office and show its statewide lines. Nevada has no Area Agencies on Aging; each county shows its Nevada Care Connection Resource Center from an October 2024 county-board presentation. Centers for Independent Living come from the ILRU national directory.
